genesis.32.p1.b1.text: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

genesis.32.p1.b3.text: “You are to say to my master Esau, ‘Your servant Jacob says: I have been staying with Laban and have remained there until now.

genesis.32.p1.b4.text: I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, menservants, and maidservants. I have sent this message to inform my master, so that I may find favor in your sight.’”

genesis.32.p2.b1.text: “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you—he and four hundred men with him.”

genesis.32.p2.b3.text: “If Esau comes and attacks one camp, then the other camp can escape.”

genesis.32.p3.b1.text: “O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac,

genesis.32.p3.b2.text: I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant. Indeed, with only my staff I came across the Jordan, but now I have become two camps.

genesis.32.p3.b3.text: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau,

genesis.32.p3.b4.text: But You have said, ‘I will surely make you prosper, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.’”

genesis.32.p4.b1.text: Jacob spent the night there, and from what he had brought with him, he selected a gift for his brother Esau:

genesis.32.p4.b2.text: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams,

genesis.32.p4.b3.text: 30 milk camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.

genesis.32.p4.b4.text: “Go on ahead of me, and keep some distance between the herds.”

genesis.32.p5.b1.text: “When my brother Esau meets you and asks, ‘To whom do you belong, where are you going, and whose animals are these before you?’

genesis.32.p5.b2.text: then you are to say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift, sent to my lord Esau. And behold, Jacob is behind us.’”

genesis.32.p5.b3.text: “I will appease Esau with the gift that is going before me. After that I can face him, and perhaps he will accept me.”

genesis.32.p5.b4.text: So Jacob’s gifts went on before him, while he spent the night in the camp.

genesis.32.p6.b1.text: During the night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

genesis.32.p6.b2.text: He took them and sent them across the stream, along with all his possessions.

genesis.32.p6.b3.text: So Jacob was left all alone,

genesis.32.p7.b1.text: there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.

genesis.32.p7.b2.text: When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob,

genesis.32.p7.b3.text: he struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled.

genesis.32.p8.b1.text: “Let me go, for it is daybreak.”

genesis.32.p8.b2.text: “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”

genesis.32.p8.b3.text: “What is your name?” the man asked. “Jacob,” he replied.

genesis.32.p8.b4.text: “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.”

genesis.32.p9.b1.text: And Jacob requested, “Please tell me your name.”

genesis.32.p9.b2.text: But he replied, “Why do you ask my name?”

genesis.32.p9.b4.text: “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”

genesis.32.p10.b1.text: The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.

genesis.32.p10.b2.text: Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon which is at the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.
